mappings.parent_claim_text: The frozen Picard/Bianchi literature identifies the geodesic object and primitive, inversion, and ideal-arithmetic vocabularies, but it does not define the project-specific Gaussian-prime-ideal owner law.
The exact level-(3) primitive, conjugacy, maximal-root, inversion, and unoriented quotient remains a composite certificate target rather than a theorem supplied by any one frozen source.
A literal single Gaussian-prime-ideal codomain is a deliberately strict frozen design frame, not an intrinsically forced codomain; any split-branch obstruction is conditional on that frame.

Mechanism admissibility under the strict codomain and primitive-unoriented quotient completeness are independent pre-performance gates, so collision-separation performance cannot select or repair either interface.
The report's contribution is a fail-closed research-design and certificate architecture that separates a conditional strict-codomain test from a genuine quotient-completeness problem.

A reproducible future implementation requires explicit object serializers, positive and negative quotient certificates, immutable mechanism registration, typed controls, and independent replay receipts.

Source identity and reference closure do not provide passage-level theorem verification because all frozen citation locators are absent and correction, retraction, and source-COI checks remain bounded or unrun.
Phase-6 report revision changes no scientific result or formal route state: the tuple remains unassigned, positive arithmetic A2 remains absent, and Route B remains closed.
